qualification_note: Diagnostic working evaluations only. This artifact cannot qualify any candidate, satisfy a holdout requirement, or become a holdout evaluation.
score_method: Weighted base plus interaction adjustment, constrained to 1-10, then rounded to one decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly isolates contract-specific producer status, exemption thresholds, pre-pickup evidence and measured-weight reconciliation rather than treating generic BDO entry as the opportunity.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Excess-weight, contamination, rejection and BDO failures can create material charges, but their frequency and contractors' willingness to fund another workflow beside cheap software or administration remain uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The modeled 63% contribution and short CAC payback are attractive if support stays low, but contribution falls near 30% with modest manual coordination and the wealth path requires roughly 2,300 active accounts.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The high-frequency installation-contractor beachhead is specific and locally accessible, although exemptions and contractual responsibility may remove many nominal prospects and no qualified segment count exists.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: RLGSOFT, Ekopomoc, Interzero and Gruz Assistance already cover inexpensive BDO administration, automation or integrated pickup, leaving a narrow and readily contestable wedge.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven workflow could extend across trades, regions, collectors and adjacent waste handoffs, but special waste regimes and local service density make expansion operationally uneven.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Outcome-linked handoff data could improve screening and estimates, but reuse rights are unresolved and incumbents could reproduce photo capture and reconciliation features.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Proof-before-pickup and surcharge evidence may outperform form-entry tools, but no evidence yet quantifies avoided cost or shows a meaningful advantage over integrated service incumbents.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2025 segregation duties, meaningful physical-service charges and available BDO API support create a timely opening, although established providers already respond to it.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer provides unusually cheap initial access, while collectors and wholesalers are plausible scalable channels; neither unrelated conversion nor partner distribution has been demonstrated.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder fits the automation work and can fund the pilot, but environmental classification, data permissions, disputes and on-call coordination threaten part-time feasibility.

assumptions: A reachable subset of contractors averages at least one non-exempt paid handoff monthly.
Contractors will pay 99 PLN monthly after savings or avoided-cost proof.
Customer-scoped BDO access can be onboarded without excessive support.
Human exception work stays near ten minutes per completed pickup.
Collectors will provide timely scale evidence and accept commercially usable terms.
evaluations.main_structural_strength: Direct access to a live renewable-installer workflow makes the legal and physical handoff problem unusually cheap to instrument and validate.
evaluations.primary_score_limiter: The frequency-qualified market, separate software budget and low-touch exception economics are all unproven while close substitutes already exist.
evaluations.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Interzero already combines pickup scheduling, BDO-connected creation and correction, reporting and expert support, while Gruz Assistance markets nationwide booking with complete BDO administration.
evaluations.highest_value_structural_change: Make two or three collectors the primary paying customers for a white-label pre-acceptance and reconciliation workflow, give contractors a lightweight interface, and charge an annual minimum plus completed-handoff fees tied to reduced exceptions.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A blinded cohort of unrelated contractors showing monthly eligible-handoff frequency and preventable loss rates.
Paid conversion and retention at the proposed contractor price.
Signed collector service, data and fee terms.
Measured CAC, support minutes, dispute cost and contribution margin outside the family relationship.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Mandatory recurring inspections and short protocol handoffs create genuine coordination work, but the managed-compliance-desk insight is already reflected in established software and nationwide service offers.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The legal obligation and a 415-object private RFP demonstrate recurring procurement pain, but no evidence shows willingness to pay a separate recurring platform and dispatch charge.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Modeled renewal contribution is 43%, but first-year contribution is only 20%, dispatch revenue on published core prices is small, and the wealth path requires about 7,000 retained buildings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Private managers with 100-plus buildings in one region form a coherent beachhead, supported by one dense buyer example, but the scalable portfolio denominator is unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Free c-KOB, Przeglądy Budynku, Figure and Mediatis collectively cover records, scheduling, multi-specialty delivery and documentation, leaving little basis for regional domination.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted portfolio workflow could expand into additional regions, specialties, defect tracking and remediation governance once embedded with managers.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Supplier-performance and protocol-quality data could improve operations, but contractual reuse is constrained, managers can bypass introductions and incumbents already possess workflow data.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Portfolio normalization and packet QA add value beyond reminders, yet Mediatis already offers a closely matching coordinated service and Figure supplies low-priced multi-specialty delivery.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Recurring statutory deadlines sustain demand, but free c-KOB and the extension of legacy-paper transition to 2031 reduce migration urgency.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A small number of portfolio managers can aggregate many buildings, but procurement authority, scalable prospecting and conversion are unverified and require relationship-heavy selling.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Multi-specialty credentialing, peak-period scheduling, protocol rework, urgent defects and technical-liability boundaries conflict materially with a solo founder's part-time availability.

assumptions: Managers can contract centrally for enough buildings without repeated community approvals.
Customers accept a separate recurring compliance-desk fee.
Coordination and QA remain below two hours per building-year.
Existing inspectors contract directly and accept standardized packet requirements.
Authorized or manual c-KOB workflows are operationally sufficient.
evaluations.main_structural_strength: One portfolio-level buyer can aggregate hundreds of legally recurring inspection events, creating concentrated demand and potentially efficient account economics.
evaluations.primary_score_limiter: Human coordination and liability are heavy relative to per-building revenue, while direct software and full-service substitutes already exist.
evaluations.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Mediatis already markets nationwide multi-specialty coordination, its own inspection application, documentation and KOB/c-KOB assistance to portfolio customers.
evaluations.highest_value_structural_change: Remove the two-sided dispatch proposition and sell an annual portfolio-level protocol-quality and exception-management retainer that works with each manager's incumbent inspectors, with a meaningful minimum contract value.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two unrelated managers signing annual minimum contracts for substantial portfolios.
Observed administrative or rework savings exceeding the fee.
Sub-two-hour operating effort and high first-pass packet completeness.
Renewal evidence, measured acquisition cost and confirmed c-KOB operating permissions.
Insured partner capacity through May and November peaks.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Tariff rules create mechanically detectable leakage, and strict high-value qualification plus independent verification is a coherent response to the weak economics of generic audits.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Recoverable charges produce direct measurable cash value and should support payment on sufficiently large sites, although the prevalence of such sites and buyer conversion remain unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The 55% modeled contribution works only with customer-funded measurement and high savings; documented modest cases are uneconomic, revenue is mostly one-time and the scale path needs very high screening throughput.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Multi-site C2x/B2x retail, HoReCa, fuel and light-industry customers form a logical segment, but no unbiased evidence establishes the share clearing the high-value gate.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A free automated audit, a local outcome-priced full-service competitor and TAURON's trusted partner offer leave little room for a dominant standalone verifier.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Portfolio monitoring could expand across tariff, capacity, reactive-power and new-equipment changes, but most initial fixes remove their own revenue trigger.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Outcome labels and parser coverage can improve qualification, but tariff logic is replicable, raw-data reuse is constrained and incumbents hold stronger customer access.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Vendor neutrality and rigorous baseline rules can improve trust, but no evidence shows customers prefer them to free audits or established remediation providers.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Technology changes, current tariff mechanics and improving CSIRE access support demand, although API access remains transitional and competitors are already active.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer and accountant or electrician referrals offer plausible entry, but qualification signals are absent from public lists and partner volume, incentives and exclusivity are unproven.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder fits tariff analysis and can fund a partner-led pilot, while electrical expertise, M&V disputes, professional liability and partner quality remain material execution burdens.

assumptions: Partner-reachable portfolios contain enough sites with at least 24,000-30,000 PLN recoverable annual value.
Customers fund measurement, verification, hardware and installation separately.
Authorized buyers accept a pre-agreed savings baseline and a 20% fee.
Referral partners supply sufficient invoice volume at a 20% revenue share.
Data exports remain usable during the CSIRE transition.
Monitoring can eventually generate recurring portfolio revenue.
evaluations.main_structural_strength: The customer benefit is directly monetary, measurable on bills and compatible with aligned outcome pricing when a high-value site is found.
evaluations.primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated economical way to find enough high-value sites before free incumbents capture them, and successful fixes are predominantly one-time.
evaluations.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: NextGen offers the invoice-layer audit free, biernaenergia.pl already combines analysis, measurement and outcome-linked remediation, and TAURON supplies an incumbent-branded full-stack alternative.
evaluations.highest_value_structural_change: Sell a CFO-level annual contract covering many PPEs, combining portfolio screening, recurring drift monitoring and a savings fee, so one acquisition yields multiple sites and recurring revenue while physical work remains customer-funded.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: An unselected invoice cohort from several unrelated partners establishing the high-value hit-rate distribution.
Authorized-signer conversion, sales-cycle and collected-fee data.
The share of savings achievable without costly measurement or hardware.
Completed-project contribution after disputes, referral shares and verification.
Paid renewal for portfolio monitoring after the initial correction.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Polish late-payment pain and KSeF coverage create a logical automation opportunity, but invoice access without reconciled payment status does not itself create a differentiated product.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Late payments are widespread, Poland is among the worst-reported markets and firms spend substantial staff time chasing cash; direct recovery and factoring vendors also evidence commercial demand.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The modeled 53% contribution and short payback depend on causal cash lift, low exception time and inexpensive connectors, while gainshare attribution, retention and the 1,200-customer scale path remain fragile.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish firms issuing 50-500 monthly invoices are a plausible recurring-use segment, but no reachable list combines invoice volume, overdue exposure, buying authority and inadequate incumbent tooling.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Comarch embeds automated dunning in the accounting workflow, Vindicat offers integrated recovery and factoring substitutes liquidity, making standalone domination implausible without exclusive distribution.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted receivables layer could expand into factoring, trade-credit insurance, collection routing and cash forecasting, subject to regulatory and partner-conflict constraints.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Incumbent ERPs already hold reconciled data, KSeF access is standardized and cross-customer learning is constrained by purpose limitation and unproven reuse rights.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Causal prioritization and relationship-sensitive escalation could improve ordinary reminders, but no Polish B2B evidence establishes incremental recovery or superiority over existing workflows.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Mandatory KSeF adoption creates a timely integration event against severe payment pain, even though it simultaneously strengthens existing accounting vendors.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accounting offices and integrators can receive delegated invoice access, but they lack inherent buying authority, may view the product as competitive and have not demonstrated conversion economics.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder fits causal analytics and automation, while payment matching, AISP dependence, GDPR, false-overdue harm and manual disputes create significant product and operating risk.

assumptions: A registered AISP or accounting connector supplies reliable reconciled status at acceptable cost.
Accounting partners accept a 20% revenue share and generate qualified clients.
The workflow creates incremental cash lift rather than merely accelerating inevitable payment.
Customers accept an auditable continuing counterfactual or flat subscription alternative.
Exception handling remains below 0.5 hour per client monthly.
Retention remains strong after receivables discipline improves.
evaluations.main_structural_strength: The opportunity addresses urgent, recurring and quantitatively measurable pain that closely matches the founder's causal-analysis and automation strengths.
evaluations.primary_score_limiter: A standalone layer lacks privileged payment data, exclusive distribution or a durable advantage over ERPs, collection platforms and factors.
evaluations.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Comarch already automates reminders, demands and sales blocking inside the system of record, while Vindicat directly offers integrated automated recovery at an advertised 8% success fee.
evaluations.highest_value_structural_change: Become a white-label prioritization and experiment module for accounting offices, ERP integrators or AISPs that already possess reconciled payment data and customer distribution, using per-entity SaaS pricing instead of disputed standalone gainshare.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed channel partner with reconciled payment access and explicit buying-distribution authority.
A randomized Polish B2B pilot demonstrating DSO and incremental-cash lift over disciplined reminders.
Observed false-overdue, complaint, dispute and relationship-loss rates.
Connector match rates, human minutes, contribution margin and CAC.
Paid partner and client retention plus lawful cross-customer learning rights.
